title: Make the caption readable
summary: Darken the bottom of a busy background so a white caption stands out.
brief: The poster has a busy striped background, and its caption is hard to read. Keep the stripes, but lay a dark fade over them: transparent until 30% of the height, then down to black at 75% opacity (rgb(0 0 0 / 0.75)) at the bottom.
Do it on .poster itself, with no extra elements.
hints: An element can have several background images at once, separated by commas.
The first image in the list is painted on top. So the fade goes first, then the stripes.
background-image: linear-gradient(transparent 30%, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.75)), repeating-linear-gradient(…the existing stripes…). Do not use opacity: it would fade the text too.

children.text: Fridays, 6pm until late, on the old harbour.

solutionNotes: background-image accepts a list of layers, and the first one is painted on top. A gradient from transparent to a semi-transparent black darkens only the bottom of the poster, where the caption sits, while the stripes still show through above. opacity would be the wrong tool: it fades the whole element, text included.
